evidenceRecords.text: The U.S. Navy is preparing to sign a contract with Lockheed Martin to integrate the stealthy AGM-158C Long Range Anti-Ship Missile (LRASM) onto the Air Force’s B-52 Stratofortress bombers, according to an October 7 government notice.

The effort would add another long-range maritime strike option to the U.S. bomber force as the military looks to counter increasingly capable adversary naval forces, especially in the Indo-Pacific theater.

U.S. Willis The latest Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) notice says the command intends to enter into sole-source negotiations with Lockheed Martin and subsequently award a cost-plus-fixed-fee delivery order covering LRASM integration on the B-52.
The B-52 can carry up to 20 JASSMs, and the weapons have the same dimensions, but the government notice does not specify how many LRASMs the bomber would ultimately carry.
A B-52 flies across the Atlantic Ocean on June 17, 2019, for a flight in support of Exercise BALTOPS 2019, the largest multinational maritime exercise of the year in the Baltic Sea.

The U.S. Air Force’s Fiscal Year 2027 budget proposal further outlines plans to integrate the latest variants of LRASM and JASSM onto the B-52, including versions not yet cleared for use on the bomber.

Planned work in FY2027 includes incorporating the missiles’ operational flight programs into the B-52’s baseline bomber software, validating safe weapon separation from both wing-mounted stations and the internal carriage launcher, updating armament interfaces, and completing system-safety testing.
Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missiles are prepared to be loaded on to a U.S. Air Force B-52 on Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, on April 24, 2023.
An AGM-158C Long Range Anti-Ship Missile is seen under the wing of an F/A-18, with another missile in the foreground.
U.S. Navy For the B-52, the addition of LRASM would provide a dedicated anti-ship weapon alongside its established land-attack arsenal.
The B-52 also has a demonstrated naval mine-laying capability through the Quickstrike family of aerial mines.

evidenceRecords.text: Electro Optic Systems Holdings Limited (EOS) has entered into an agreement with the government of a Middle Eastern Gulf state (a Gulf Co-operation Council member) for the provision of a nationwide, counter-uncrewed aerial system (C-UAS) defence system valued at GBP 370 million.
EOS said on 9 October that this is the largest contract the company has secured.
The company’s NiDAR C-UAS system, acquired as part of the recent MARSS acquisition, is central to the contract.
It is an AI-enabled command and control system (C2), designed specifically for C-UAS defence, covering both airborne and coastal seaborne drone detection.
The contract requires the rapid deployment of a cellular, nationwide C-UAS system with NiDAR C2.
EOS is acting as the prime contractor and systems integrator.

“In alignment with the President’s National Space Policy, NASA is committed to maintaining a sustained American presence in low Earth orbit long after the International Space Station retires,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.

Commercial space stations may provide that capability while creating new opportunities for American industry and allowing NASA to concentrate more of our resources on the near-impossible missions ahead.” Building on the agency’s Ignition event earlier this year, NASA regularly has engaged with private industry to shape the agency’s future direction in low Earth orbit.
This included publishing two Requests for Information in March to gather industry’s perspective on low Earth orbit destinations and transportation.

The agency also published a draft Request for Proposals in July, followed by an industry day and one-on-one meetings that allowed interested companies to review and comment on the planned acquisition approach.
“We’ve made it clear that NASA will never give up its presence in low Earth orbit,” said Isaacman.
“Since Ignition, we have spent a lot of time listening to industry and working through what it will take to make this transition successful.

We want to see credible plans, strong technical execution, and companies prepared to invest in destinations that can serve NASA while developing additional customers and markets of their own.” Proposals are due Tuesday, Dec. 8, with contract awards expected in spring 2027.

Learn more about NASA’s missions on the agency’s website: https://www.nasa.gov -end- George Alderman / Joshua Finch Headquarters, Washington 202-358-1600 george.c.alderman@nasa.gov / joshua.a.finch@nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Oct 09, 2026 Editor Jessica Taveau Location NASA Headquarters Related Terms Commercial Space Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate Low Earth Orbit Economy

items.title: Three Saudi nationals killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport
items.originalTitle: Three Saudi nationals killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport
items.summary: Three Saudi Arabian nationals have been killed in two attacks on the international airport in the capital, Riyadh, the country's civil aviation authority has said, after Yemen's Houthis said they had targeted the facility. The attacks also resulted in "injuries to a number of Saudi citizens and residents of various nationalities", the General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement on X. It added that the first attack on Thursday targeted the airport while the second had struck an aircraft belonging to state carrier Saudia.

evidenceRecords.text: Three Saudi Arabian nationals have been killed in two attacks on the international airport in the capital, Riyadh, the country's civil aviation authority has said, after Yemen's Houthis said they had targeted the facility.
The attacks also resulted in "injuries to a number of Saudi citizens and residents of various nationalities", the General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement on X.
It added that the first attack on Thursday targeted the airport while the second had struck an aircraft belonging to state carrier Saudia.
One of its pilots was among those killed, the airline said in a statement.
Air traffic had returned to normal, the civil aviation authority said.
Yemen's Houthi group said on Thursday it had attacked the airport with two ballistic missiles.
The Iran-aligned group said it had also targeted an airport in Najran city near the Saudi border with Yemen, and Khamis Mushait air base further north.
Saudi Arabia has not confirmed these attacks.
The latest casualties follow the deaths of three people in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October.
Two were killed and 28 wounded in an attack at Abha International Airport, the civil aviation body said on Wednesday.
Another person was killed at King Khalid airport in Riyadh.
The latest attacks come amid a marked escalation in renewed fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country's north-west.

items.summary: Insider Brief izmo Microsystems and IIT Madras have entered Phase II of the Centre for Programmable Photonic Integrated Circuits and Systems (CPPICS), a five-year silicon photonics program with a total outlay of ₹99.94 crore. The SPECTRA program will target silicon photonics applications in data-center transceivers, microwave photonics, quantum technologies and photonic computing for AI. izmo Microsystems will contribute packaging, testing and integration expertise, including work on co-packaged optics and a 1.6 Tbps silicon photonics transceiver engine.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief izmo Microsystems and IIT Madras have entered Phase II of the Centre for Programmable Photonic Integrated Circuits and Systems (CPPICS), a five-year silicon photonics program with a total outlay of ₹99.94 crore.

The SPECTRA program will target silicon photonics applications in data-center transceivers, microwave photonics, quantum technologies and photonic computing for AI. izmo Microsystems will contribute packaging, testing and integration expertise, including work on co-packaged optics and a 1.6 Tbps silicon photonics transceiver engine.
PRESS RELEASE — izmo Limited (NSE: IZMO) (BSE: 532341) today announced that its semiconductor subsidiary, izmo Microsystems Pvt.

Ltd., has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) for Phase II of the Centre for Programmable Photonic Integrated Circuits and Systems (CPPICS).

The Phase II program, titled Silicon Photonics Enabled Cutting-edge Technology Research and Applications (SPECTRA) , has been sanctioned by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, with a total project outlay of ₹99.94 crore.
The five-year program includes a MeitY contribution of ₹97.54 crore and a ₹2.40 crore cash and in-kind commitment from izmo Microsystems.

CPPICS Phase II is designed to advance silicon photonics technologies from research towards commercially deployable products, covering photonic integrated circuit design, fabrication, characterization, advanced packaging, testing and system integration.
Silicon Photonics for the AI infrastructure era The program comes at a time when optical connectivity is becoming critical infrastructure for AI and high-performance computing.

The program also proposes development of a silicon photonics Process Design Kit incorporating more than 100 IP blocks for 200 mm wafer platforms, supporting the design and manufacture of increasingly complex photonic integrated circuits. izmo Microsystems to Drive Packaging and Industrialization A key challenge in silicon photonics is converting a fabricated photonic chip into a reliable and manufacturable optical system.
CPPICS Phase II brings together IIT Madras’ silicon photonics research capabilities with izmo Microsystems’ advanced packaging and manufacturing expertise.

items.summary: Standing on the deck of the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln , Secretary Pete Hegseth looked up at the flattop’s superstructure and got a good indication of many of the targets the Lincoln Carrier Strike Group (CSG) destroyed during its six-month fight with Iran . In a photograph shared by the Pentagon’s image distribution site, Hegseth is seen examining a wall of so-called kill marks stenciled onto the superstructure.

evidenceRecords.text: Standing on the deck of the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln , Secretary Pete Hegseth looked up at the flattop’s superstructure and got a good indication of many of the targets the Lincoln Carrier Strike Group (CSG) destroyed during its six-month fight with Iran .
In a photograph shared by the Pentagon’s image distribution site, Hegseth is seen examining a wall of so-called kill marks stenciled onto the superstructure.
By our count from the image and a video taken during Hegseth’s visit, both of which you can see below, there are 103 one-way attack (OWA) drone kill marks and 34 ship kill marks.
It is unclear whether there are other kill marks we can’t see.
Though they resemble Shahed-136s, which are the most notorious of Iranian OWA drones, these silhouettes would represent all types shot down, and Iran has many.

Madelyn Keech To the sailors of the USS ABRAHAM LINCOLN— WELCOME HOME pic.twitter.com/AoQymN2yfZ — Secretary of War Pete Hegseth (@SecWar) October 7, 2026 On board to welcome the ship and its crew as it headed back to its home port of San Diego after a tumultuous and historic deployment, Hegseth extolled the strike group’s accomplishments.

Defense Secretary @PeteHegseth awards Presidential Unit Citation to USS Abraham Lincoln pic.twitter.com/DbS5YYu9oB — CSPAN (@cspan) October 7, 2026 It is unclear at the moment why there are at least 26 more drone kill marks stenciled onto the Lincoln than the number of drones shot down listed in the unit citation and why there are 30 fewer ship kill marks than the tally noted in the citation.

items.summary: Insider Brief BTQ Technologies has partnered with MoonPay Korea to secure its Korean won-backed stablecoin infrastructure, with a focus on post-quantum cryptography (PQC). The companies plan to develop a post-quantum security roadmap and test BTQ ’s Quantum Secure Stablecoin Network (QSSN) with Korean banking institutions. The companies plan to develop a post-quantum security roadmap and test BTQ ’s Quantum Secure Stablecoin Network (QSSN) with Korean banking institutions.

PRESS RELEASE — BTQ Technologies Corp. ( “ BTQ “ or the “Company” ) (Nasdaq: BTQ ) (CBOE CA: BTQ), a global technology company building the trust infrastructure for the quantum era, has announced a strategic partnership with MoonPay Korea, part of MoonPay Inc. (“MoonPay”), the leading global crypto payments network.
Under the partnership, BTQ will serve as the security partner for MoonPay Korea’s stablecoin infrastructure in Korea, with a focus on post-quantum cryptography (“PQC”).

MoonPay Korea is building full-stack on-chain infrastructure for Korea’s emerging won-backed stablecoin market, covering issuance support, distribution, wallet access, settlement, and currency conversion through to last-mile delivery to users and merchants.
The partnership brings BTQ into one of the most innovative infrastructure efforts in Korea’s stablecoin market and connects it to a global network.

MoonPay Korea links Korean won-backed stablecoins to that network for distribution, cross-border settlement, and wallet access, so the infrastructure BTQ helps secure in Korea is designed to reach users and merchants worldwide.

BTQ and MoonPay Korea will jointly develop a post-quantum security roadmap for MoonPay Korea’s stablecoin infrastructure, covering a cryptographic inventory, risk prioritization, and a phased migration plan.

Through MoonPay Korea, BTQ will run a proof of concept of its Quantum Secure Stablecoin Network (“QSSN”) with Korean banking institutions, testing quantum-safe transaction signing and key management across the wallet and settlement infrastructure behind Korea’s won-backed stablecoins.
The companies will work on post-quantum readiness across each layer of MoonPay Korea’s infrastructure, from issuance and distribution to wallets and last-mile delivery.
BTQ will work alongside MoonPay Korea and its banking and institutional partners to support quantum-safe standards for Korea’s won-backed stablecoin ecosystem.

evidenceRecords.text: A new U.S. Army poster depicts a soldier of the Iranian army.
The graphics show a bearded soldier wearing sunglasses and a beret, with captions describing the various weapons he might carry and the uniforms he might wear.
That the U.S. Army has a quick-recognition guide for Iranian soldiers doesn’t mean America will invade Iran.
The Army’s Training and Transformation Command has a library of graphical recognition posters for the armies of various nations, including China’s People’s Liberation Army .

The Artesh soldier in the U.S. Army poster — wearing the green beret of the Iranian special forces — doesn’t appear much different than the infantry in many other armies, with a mix of Soviet, Western and Iranian gear.
The Army’s Training and Transformation Command has a library of graphical recognition posters for the armies of various nations, including China’s People’s Liberation Army.
The new guide, published Sept. 24, isn’t focused on the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the praetorian guard of the Iranian regime that grabs most of the headlines.
The IRGC controls many of the weapons that have been fired at American forces and Iran’s neighbors, including ballistic missiles, drones and fast-attack boats.
Instead, the U.S. Army guide displays a soldier of the Islamic Republic of Iran Army, also known as Artesh.

It is a mainly conscript force of 350,000 personnel that is essentially the regular armed forces of the nation of Iran, including armored, infantry, special forces, air defense, aircraft and naval units, according to the research organization the Institute for the Study of War.
In contrast, the IRGC protects an Iranian regime that doesn’t fully trust the regular armed forces, which date back to the days of the Shah.
As in many authoritarian nations, such as Saddam Hussein’s Iraq, there is a deliberate rivalry between the regular and politicized armed forces, with the regime’s pet army getting the best equipment.
He is shown carrying an AKM, Masaf-2 or Heckler & Koch G3A6 rifle.
He can also be armed with an MG3 machine gun or an RPG-7, plus grenades, body armor, rucksack, canteen and gas mask, among other gear.
The image shows five different camouflage uniforms, including khaki and woodland, as well as three camouflage patterns for the special forces.

items.title: Technology Used by Optical Atomic Clocks May Jump From Lab to Consumer
items.originalTitle: Technology Used by Optical Atomic Clocks May Jump From Lab to Consumer
items.summary: Insider Brief University of Auckland and U.S. researchers demonstrated a chip-based optical frequency comb that could support smaller precision measurement systems, including portable atomic clocks. The researchers demonstrated precise optical frequency generation, low-noise millimetre-wave signals and optical clock readout, with potential applications in navigation, telecommunications and sensing. So far, the laser tools called optical frequency combs have been trapped in the lab because of their size and expense.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief University of Auckland and U.S. researchers demonstrated a chip-based optical frequency comb that could support smaller precision measurement systems, including portable atomic clocks.

The researchers demonstrated precise optical frequency generation, low-noise millimetre-wave signals and optical clock readout, with potential applications in navigation, telecommunications and sensing.
So far, the laser tools called optical frequency combs have been trapped in the lab because of their size and expense.
Optical frequency combs are the standard tools for measuring the frequency – or colours – of light.

But research by University of Auckland and US scientists, reported in the prestigious journal Nature, suggests a new path for shrinking the technology to chip size for future navigation systems, communications networks, precision sensors and portable atomic clocks.

The breakthrough is a culmination of work that started in 2021, when Professor Miro Erkintalo, who is the head of the Department of Physics at the University and a researcher at the Dodd-Walls Centre for Photonic and Quantum Technologies, began exploring a potential new way to generate chip-scale frequency combs.
With the help of his students, he predicted that two laser beams launched into a chip-scale ring could generate a new type of frequency comb.

The prediction became reality in 2024, when the Auckland researchers teamed up with Grégory Moille and Kartik Srinivasan from the University of Maryland and the US National Institute of Science and Technology to successfully demonstrate the idea in the lab.
While the 2024 demonstration was a groundbreaking physics proof-of-concept, breakthrough applications were still unrealized.
Optical frequency combs have enabled the creation of the most precise clocks in the world – optical atomic clocks – and the many other applications have included experiments in basic physics.
Portable optical atomic clocks could help map underground variations in mineral deposits and enable navigation systems that don’t rely on GPS satellite signals.

Reducing the size, weight, power, and cost of optical frequency combs can lead to mass production and move the technology from lab to consumer, Erkintalo and his collaborators write in the Nature paper.

items.originalTitle: Army’s new command plans to streamline autonomous warfare acquisition
items.summary: The service announced the creation of Futures and Autonomous Systems Command on Friday, a day after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the creation of a new combatant command for autonomous warfare in a speech to troops. "Secretary Hegseth made it clear: We are done with the bureaucratic inertia holding back modernization,” acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said in a news release . FASCOM will stand up in the wake of last year’s decision to consolidate Army Futures Command and Training and Doctrine Command , part of a multi-year effort by the service to reduce its general officer ranks .

evidenceRecords.text: The service announced the creation of Futures and Autonomous Systems Command on Friday, a day after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the creation of a new combatant command for autonomous warfare in a speech to troops.
"Secretary Hegseth made it clear: We are done with the bureaucratic inertia holding back modernization,” acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said in a news release .

FASCOM will stand up in the wake of last year’s decision to consolidate Army Futures Command and Training and Doctrine Command , part of a multi-year effort by the service to reduce its general officer ranks .
The difference is that FASCOM will be led by an acquisition executive, where Futures Command had four-star generals with infantry backgrounds at the helm during its short tenure.

Though the command endeavoured to fix the Army’s broken requirements process, ultimately the final decisions and acquisitions were made at the Pentagon, creating a disconnect that FASCOM won’t have to deal with.
Except this time, rather than a standalone four-star command with no joint equivalent, FASCOM could nest under the new Autonomous Warfare Command as a service component.
\"Secretary Hegseth made it clear: We are done with the bureaucratic inertia holding back modernization,\u201d acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said in a news release.\u00a0

FASCOM will stand up in the wake of last year\u2019s decision to consolidate Army Futures Command and Training and Doctrine Command, part of a multi-year effort by the service to reduce its general officer ranks.
Hegseth has since taken the idea military-wide.

Though the command endeavoured to fix the Army\u2019s broken requirements process, ultimately the final decisions and acquisitions were made at the Pentagon, creating a disconnect that FASCOM won\u2019t have to deal with.
\u201cSo maybe this is kind of Futures Command 2.0, right?\u201d John G.
Ferrari, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute and retired two-star general, told Defense One.

\u201cI think their theory of the case is that you have too many disparate organizations within the Pentagon working this, and that they're working in some cases counter to each other,\u201d Ferrari said, referring to the Defense Innovation Unit, various service PAEs and the recently created Defense Autonomous Warfare Group.

A combatant command \u201cgives a single military leader the authority, the responsibility, and the resources to drive this,\u201d he said. \u201cSo I think it's an admission that the current organizational structure isn't going to deliver in a timely manner.\u201d

In August, the Department of the Navy’s Portfolio Acquisition Executive (Aviation) Rapid Capability Cell [PAE(A) RCC], in partnership with the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU), announced a separate $50 million funding action for X-BAT under the Runway Independent Maritime Expeditionary Strike (RIMES) effort.
This action was a separate prior modification to the existing OT agreement referenced here.
Shield AI independently committed $50 million of private capital alongside that effort.

Across the broader X-BAT program, a team of 500 engineers at Shield AI and key suppliers, including GE Aerospace, is building flight-test aircraft.
Shield AI’s Hivemind software serves as X-BAT’s AI pilot, enabling operations in GPS-denied and communications-constrained conditions.
“We are testing early and often while working on the aircraft, mission systems, ship suitability and production in parallel,” said Armor Harris, senior vice president of aircraft at Shield AI.

“That approach helps us identify and resolve issues earlier, reduce development risk and move more quickly toward flight testing.” X-BAT is scheduled to begin flight testing later this year and is a component of DIU’s RIMES Project, a multifaceted effort across industry intended to provide Combatant Commanders with long range strike assets capable of taking off and landing vertically from ships, islands and austere sites, extending strategic reach of surface and expeditionary assets without dependence on fixed runways.

items.summary: Exail introduced its Neptis uncrewed maritime surveillance system during the Euronaval press tour. Bringing together Oryx-family uncrewed surface vessels (USVs), mission-specific sensors and command-and-control software, the system can be configured for maritime surveillance, anti-submarine warfare and the protection of critical underwater infrastructure. Exail describes Neptis as a “system of systems” designed to support persistent operations in maritime areas where access is restricted or the threat level is high.

evidenceRecords.text: Exail introduced its Neptis uncrewed maritime surveillance system during the Euronaval press tour.

Bringing together Oryx-family uncrewed surface vessels (USVs), mission-specific sensors and command-and-control software, the system can be configured for maritime surveillance, anti-submarine warfare and the protection of critical underwater infrastructure.
Exail describes Neptis as a “system of systems” designed to support persistent operations in maritime areas where access is restricted or the threat level is high.
Oryx vessels carry sensors into the area of operations, while Neptis command-and-control software manages platform supervision and communications and presents collected information to operators.

Software interface of the Neptis system (Exail picture) The demonstrated capabilities were limited to platform supervision, tactical track visualisation, operator-led preliminary assessment and intelligence support.
Neptis’ intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance missions include monitoring sea lines of communication, strategic passages, ports and exclusive economic zone boundaries.
Data from radar, electro-optical/infrared, Automatic Identification System and electronic warfare sensors can contribute to the surface picture and help identify unusual behaviour.
For anti-submarine warfare, Oryx vessels can be equipped with acoustic payloads suited to the mission.
Options include the use of towed sensors and links with other underwater assets.

Exail says this configuration can extend the acoustic sensor field and support early detection, while allowing crewed anti-submarine warfare units to conduct classification, tracking and response tasks.
The critical underwater infrastructure protection mission covers surveillance around subsea cables, pipelines, offshore energy installations and sensitive seabed infrastructure.
Depending on the selected configuration, the system can combine a persistent surface presence with underwater sensing, anomaly detection and coordination with other uncrewed assets.

items.title: Pentagon barred Qatar base access to hide Iran war damage, US senator claims
items.originalTitle: Pentagon barred Qatar base access to hide Iran war damage, US senator claims
items.summary: A U.S. senator was recently denied access to the largest military installation in the Middle East, calling it a “cover-up” over the damage suffered during the Iran war . Chris Murphy, D-Conn., visited the Middle East this week on a Congressional Delegation trip, speaking with Gulf region leaders and visiting American facilities to assess damage done by the Iran war. Murphy was denied access to Al Udeid Air Base , Qatar, which had suffered damage from drone strikes during the conflict.

evidenceRecords.text: A U.S. senator was recently denied access to the largest military installation in the Middle East, calling it a “cover-up” over the damage suffered during the Iran war .
Chris Murphy, D-Conn., visited the Middle East this week on a Congressional Delegation trip, speaking with Gulf region leaders and visiting American facilities to assess damage done by the Iran war.
Murphy was denied access to Al Udeid Air Base , Qatar, which had suffered damage from drone strikes during the conflict.

“They are using every tool they can, including withholding information about damages, slow walking the pace of reports about casualties and denying us access to see the damage as part of a campaign of cover-up, so as to mask the true cost of the war,” Murphy told reporters on Thursday.

The “unprecedented” base denial prepared Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and Defense Appropriations Committee, in the coming days to draft language that would explicitly require the Department of Defense to grant members of Congress access to military bases overseas under all circumstances if needed.
Prior to his trip, Murphy requested access to the base through a letter and direct appeal to U.S. Central Command leadership.
But he was denied access even as the Department of State supported his trip to the region, with the Defense Department saying it was due to previously imposed travel restrictions.

“Senator Murphy’s office was informed before his trip to the Middle East that he would not receive Department of War support to access Al Udeid Air Base, consistent with the Secretary of War’s directive on travel restrictions in the region ordered on March 3, 2026,” a senior Defense Department official told Military Times on Thursday.
“That decision was communicated in advance by the Office of the Secretary of War for Legislative Affairs,” the official continued.

“The Department applies the Secretary’s guidance evenly.” In early March, the State and Defense departments issued travel guidance, calling on Americans to depart areas in the region and updating its travel advisory to recommend against visiting certain countries, including Qatar.

items.title: Gaza ceasefire ‘exists in name only’, more than 100 NGOs say
items.originalTitle: Gaza ceasefire ‘exists in name only’, more than 100 NGOs say
items.summary: One year after the so-called ceasefire in Gaza was reached with United States backing, it exists only on paper, according to more than 100 humanitarian, human rights and civil society organisations. “The ceasefire exists in name only, with Israeli forces continuing to kill and injure Palestinians daily, and restrictions on aid, equipment and rebuilding materials preventing families from recovering,” a joint statement by the NGOs said on Friday.

evidenceRecords.text: One year after the so-called ceasefire in Gaza was reached with United States backing, it exists only on paper, according to more than 100 humanitarian, human rights and civil society organisations.

“The ceasefire exists in name only, with Israeli forces continuing to kill and injure Palestinians daily, and restrictions on aid, equipment and rebuilding materials preventing families from recovering,” a joint statement by the NGOs said on Friday.

Amnesty International, the Norwegian Refugee Council, Save the Children, Oxfam, Greenpeace and dozens of other international groups said Israeli attacks in the enclave have killed more than 1,400 Palestinians, including at least 327 children, in the year since US President Trump announced a deal to end hostilities as part of the Gaza Board of Peace framework.

“It is utterly shameful that a full year after the ceasefire was signed, so little has improved for Palestinians in Gaza,” Jan Egeland, secretary-general of the Norwegian Refugee Council, said in the joint statement.
Inger Ashing, chief executive of Save the Children, said, “A ceasefire is meaningless if children are still being killed and families are still unable to rebuild their lives.”

In the three years since Israel’s October 2023 genocidal war began, more than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed and 175,000 others wounded – about one in every 13 people in Gaza – according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

Gaza’s few remaining health facilities are overwhelmed and have dwindling supplies, and none of its 36 hospitals is operating at full capacity, with widespread shortages of medicine, equipment and fuel, Friday’s ministry statement said.
Almost 2 million Palestinians in the enclave are also in desperate need of shelter, where 80 percent of structures are damaged, the statement said.
Norwegian Refugee Council’s Egeland warned that restrictions on equipment and construction materials continue to prevent recovery.
“Israeli restrictions are still preventing the required equipment or materials, which are the only ways for communities to begin rebuilding their lives,” he said.
At the same time, 1.4 million people in Gaza are “facing crisis-level hunger or worse through the end of the year”, the statement added.

items.title: IonQ Demonstrates 1,000 Entanglement Events per Second in Quantum Interconnect
items.originalTitle: IonQ Demonstrates 1,000 Entanglement Events per Second in Quantum Interconnect
items.summary: Insider Brief IonQ has demonstrated entanglement rates exceeding 1,000 events per second between a trapped-ion qubit and a silicon-vacancy solid-state quantum memory using a photonic interconnect. The company says the result is more than four times faster than the previous trapped-ion interconnect record and could support distributed quantum computing. The work supports IonQ ’s participation in DARPA’s HARQ program and builds on commercial quantum networking system sales to the University of Maryland and South Korea’s SDT.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief IonQ has demonstrated entanglement rates exceeding 1,000 events per second between a trapped-ion qubit and a silicon-vacancy solid-state quantum memory using a photonic interconnect.
The company says the result is more than four times faster than the previous trapped-ion interconnect record and could support distributed quantum computing.
The work supports IonQ ’s participation in DARPA’s HARQ program and builds on commercial quantum networking system sales to the University of Maryland and South Korea’s SDT.

PRESS RELEASE — IonQ (NYSE: IONQ), the world’s leading full-stack quantum platform and foundry, today announced the achievement of entanglement rates above 1,000 per second (1 kHz) between a trapped ion qubit and a solid-state memory, through a photonic interconnect.
Entanglement is the quantum connection that lets separate systems work together, and it is the essential ingredient for networking quantum computers.
“ IonQ has crossed a pivotal milestone for memory enhanced quantum interconnects, achieving more than 1,000 entanglement events per second,” said Niccolo de Masi, Chairman and CEO of IonQ.

This breakthrough addresses a critical interconnect bottleneck and advances IonQ’s roadmap to build the networked quantum data centers of the future.” A technical paper presents results from real-world hardware testing of an end-to-end link between a trapped ion system and a silicon vacancy (SiV) qubit, building on IonQ ’s SiV quantum memory platform .
“This work shows that a photonic quantum interconnect need not be a bottleneck for distributed quantum computing,” said Mihir Bhaskar, IonQ SVP and GM of Quantum Technologies at SkyWater.

“Our technology can interface with almost any qubit type, so we see this unlocking a wide range of opportunities across multiple hardware modalities, from modular computing to networked sensing and beyond.” This quantum memory and interconnect approach is also driving IonQ ’s work with the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency’s ( DARPA) HARQ program , which seeks to develop high-speed quantum interconnects compatible with multiple computing qubit types.

IonQ ’s memory and interconnect platform is likewise ramping up commercially, with the first commercial sale to the University of Maryland announced in April, and a second system sale to SDT in South Korea, announced in September.

PRESS RELEASE — Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative announces seventeen professionals from sixteen Tennessee employers completed the Quantum Ready Pre-Apprenticeship, a 12-week program created by the Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative (CQC) to help companies understand emerging quantum technologies.

The program was designed for professionals already working in technology-adjacent roles, with two goals: upskilling the existing workforce and building quantum proficiency inside the organizations where they work.
“Quantum won’t replace every system overnight, but exploring where it complements classical technology can provide businesses an early, distinct competitive edge,” said Charlie Brock, CEO of CQC.

“This program puts early advocates directly into the companies best positioned to benefit, equipping them to test real-world quantum applications and address complex business challenges classical computing alone can’t resolve.” “Research opens the door to new possibilities, and industry adoption carries that work into economic impact,” said Mina Sartipi, Interim Vice Chancellor for Research at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga .

Every trip or vehicle you add multiplies the number of possible schedules, so I identified where quantum optimization could come in once current methods reach their limits.” The Quantum Ready Pre-Apprenticeship was delivered through the BuildWithin platform and supported by a National Science Foundation planning grant awarded to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga , with CQC serving as a subawardee focused on workforce and industry engagement.

Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, injuring another 32.

PRESS RELEASE — Quantum Elements , developers of software shortening the path to fault-tolerant quantum computing, today announced that its Constellation platform has been named a winner of TMCnet’z inaugural 2026 Quantum Computing Product of the Year Awards.
Constellation gives quantum teams a hardware-aware development environment, running on classical computer architecture, to design, test and analyze quantum systems before committing to hardware runs.
It allows quantum hardware teams to understand noise, test error-correction strategies, and evaluate decoder performance.

“Constellation is bridging the gap between experimental hardware to fault-tolerant system design by giving development teams a faster, safer, and more repeatable way to validate ideas, improve designs, and prepare workflows for real-world deployment,” said Izhar Medalsy, co-founder and CEO of Quantum Elements .

“We are honored by this recognition of the important role we are playing in advancing towards fault-tolerant quantum computers.” “On behalf of TMCnet and our editors, I’m pleased to recognize Quantum Elements as a winner of the inaugural 2026 Quantum Computing Product of the Year Awards,” said Rich Tehrani, TMCnet’s CEO and Group Editor-in-Chief.

“Constellation represents the kind of innovation that is helping move quantum computing forward—from extraordinary science toward technologies that organizations can access, develop and ultimately put to work.

We congratulate Quantum Elements on this achievement and are proud to recognize it as part of the first class of Quantum Computing Product of the Year Award winners.” The Quantum Computing Product of the Year Awards recognize outstanding products and solutions advancing the quantum computing ecosystem and helping move quantum applications and broader commercial adoption.
Winners of the 2026 Quantum Computing Product of the Year Awards are published on TMCnet.

The 4th Multi-Domain Task Force will focus on synchronizing long-range precision fires in the Indo-Pacific region “to deny, disrupt and disaggregate adversary capabilities” and create advantages for other units in the joint force, the Army said in a release. evidenceRecords.text: A new U.S. Army multi-domain task force, one of five recently established or under development by the service, was activated this week with a ceremony at Fort Carson, Colorado.

The 4th Multi-Domain Task Force will focus on synchronizing long-range precision fires in the Indo-Pacific region “to deny, disrupt and disaggregate adversary capabilities” and create advantages for other units in the joint force, the Army said in a release.
The task force includes four battalions and is planned to grow to 2,100 soldiers.

In June, the Army combined the 7th Infantry Division and the 1st Multi-Domain Task Force at Lewis-McChord into the 7th Infantry Division (Multi-Domain Command-Pacific) , which serves as the multi-domain operational headquarters.

The establishment of the 7th Infantry Division (Multi-Domain Command-Pacific) and the 4th Multi-Domain Task Force are part of a broader transformation initiative “to counter near-peer adversaries in an increasingly complex global landscape,” the Army said.
The initiative includes the service establishing five multi-domain task forces by 2028, according to a Congressional Research Service report .
The Army activated the 2nd Multi-Domain Task Force in 2021 at the Clay Kaserne installation in Germany, and stood up the third in Hawaii in 2022.
Col. Hugh W.A. Jones assumed command of the task force during Thursday’s ceremony.
He previously commanded the 2nd Stryker Brigade, 4th Infantry Division at Fort Carson, leading the brigade when it deployed to the U.S.-Mexico border last year.
The task force reports to the 7th Infantry Division at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington.

In June, the Army combined the 7th Infantry Division and the 1st Multi-Domain Task Force at Lewis-McChord into the 7th Infantry Division (Multi-Domain Command-Pacific), which serves as the multi-domain operational headquarters.

Its mission is to integrate “maneuver, fires, air defense, cyber, space, electronic warfare, intelligence, unmanned systems, sustainment and command-and -control in support of the joint force across the Pacific,” the Army said in a release.
Gen. Bernard Harrington, commander of the 7th Infantry Division, attended the activation ceremony at Fort Carson.

“You are driving the change our nation demands today, to meet the changing character of war, to prevent conflict, and to maintain a free and open Pacific alongside our allies and partners,” Harrington told soldiers assigned to the new multi-domain task force.
The initiative includes the service establishing five multi-domain task forces by 2028, according to a Congressional Research Service report.

items.summary: Noise has long-been a complaint when it comes to public acceptance of drone operations. FFSI also noted that respondents did not evaluate drone use cases in isolation. “When asked to reason about medical, police and commercial delivery drone use together, as parts of a single emerging system, support does not simply accumulate from the most popular use cases outward,” FFSI explained.

evidenceRecords.text: Noise has long-been a complaint when it comes to public acceptance of drone operations.
FFSI also noted that respondents did not evaluate drone use cases in isolation.

“When asked to reason about medical, police and commercial delivery drone use together, as parts of a single emerging system, support does not simply accumulate from the most popular use cases outward,” FFSI explained.

“Instead, a meaningful proportion of the public who recognise clear benefits in specific applications nonetheless judge that the overall balance of benefits and drawbacks is unfavourable once the full system is considered, and association with less trusted or less clearly necessary applications – such as some commercial delivery uses that were viewed as more frivolous – can actively undermine support for more beneficial ones, including medical and emergency use.” This finding directly challenges assumptions underpinning the ‘drones for good’ argument and indicates that public trust must be
FFSI found that the UK public is “broadly supportive, engaged and discerning, rather than simply optimistic or resistant”.

There is public support for drone operations and this can be strong but also conditional on transparency, proportionality, genuine accountability, cross-sector coordination and meaningful involvement in how these systems are designed and deployed.

To address the survey’s findings, FFSI has set out five recommendations: Establish transparent and accountable oversight structures, closing current gaps between regulators and creating genuine mechanisms for citizen input and establishing new oversight mechanisms where existing bodies were not designed to cover the range of concerns, issues or risks that emerging drone systems and services present.
Deliver early and meaningful public engagement that feeds into real decisions at both local and national levels.

items.originalTitle: Quobly and SiPearl Partner to Explore European CPU-QPU Integration For Sovereign Quantum Computing
items.summary: Insider Brief Quobly and SiPearl signed a non-exclusive agreement to explore combining silicon spin quantum processors with European CPUs to support a sovereign European quantum computing system. evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Quobly and SiPearl signed a non-exclusive agreement to explore combining silicon spin quantum processors with European CPUs to support a sovereign European quantum computing system.

The initial phase will assess integrating SiPearl ’s Rhea1 CPU and Seine reference server with a Quobly quantum processor system for its Alloy product line, followed by exploration of hybrid computing workloads and future architectures.

PRESS RELEASE — Quobly , a French quantum computing company developing industrially scalable quantum computers based on silicon spin qubits, and SiPearl , the designer of European high-performance energy-efficient CPUs for sovereign supercomputing, AI and data centre, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to combine their respective technologies and expertise towards a sovereign quantum computing solution, bringing together SiPearl ’s CPU technology and Quobly ’s quantum processors.

Integrating European CPU and quantum technologies This non-exclusive collaboration will initially focus on integrating SiPearl ’s first-generation Rhea1 CPU and its associated Seine reference server with a Quobly QPU system, as part of the development of Quobly’s Alloy product line.

Supporting a European sovereign computing ecosystem The collaboration brings together two core building blocks for European computing, combining SiPearl ’s CPU technology with Quobly ’s quantum processors, and marks a first step towards bridging Europe’s HPC and quantum computing ecosystems.
SiPearl and Quobly also intend to coordinate their efforts to respond to European calls for tenders, including potential joint opportunities under the Chips Joint Undertaking (Chips JU) on Quantum.

By exploring the integration of SiPearl ’s CPU technology with our quantum computers, we are looking at how HPC and quantum computing can work together efficiently, from the system level to future architectures.

“We have had close ties with Quobly for a long time, thanks in particular to SiPearl ’s R&D centre in Grenoble, but above all because we share the same vision regarding the need to build a European hardware ecosystem for sovereign computing.

This first partnership with a quantum expert marks another significant milestone in the development of this ecosystem which will offer complementary sovereign hardware solutions in the fields of HPC, AI and quantum computing for Europe’s strategic applications”, concluded Philippe Notton, CEO and Founder of SiPearl.

Anthropic is adding dynamic workflows to its Claude Managed Agents, bringing multi-agent orchestration to the platform.
The managed agent infrastructure has been around for a while, but dynamic workflows are new.
A lead agent creates a plan, distributes tasks to sub-agents, and merges the results when they're done.
Up to 1,000 agents can run in parallel per execution.
Whether this is cost-effective seems debatable.

A senior OpenAI engineer recently called agent swarms a massive waste of tokens, but Anthropic points to its own testing: The team hid 70 bugs in a 116,000-line codebase and found that a single agent caught between 14 and 27 per run, while the dynamic workflow consistently hit 66.
Whether those gains hold across different task types remains to be seen, so, as always, it's worth testing with your own workloads.
To activate dynamic workflows, select the "multiagent_20261001" agent type.
Because these workflows can burn through "a lot of tokens," Anthropic recommends starting small.
You can get going through the documentation or by running "/claude-api managed-agents-onboard" in Claude Code.

evidenceRecords.text: Navantia and L&T (Larsen and Toubro) have reached a strategic agreement to collaborate on the upcoming program for four amphibious assault ships for the Indian Navy (known as the LPD program in India).
Navantia press release The alliance, formalized in Madrid with the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU), establishes a framework for long-term collaboration between the two companies.

The collaboration will combine L&T ‘s engineering excellence with Navantia’s experience in the design and construction of surface ships and submarines, and will contribute to the development of local capabilities for the construction of large ships, while strengthening the proposal by drawing on Navantia’s extensive experience.
Navantia has extensive experience in LHD vessels, such as the Juan Carlos I for the Spanish Navy and the Canberra and Adelaide for the Royal Australian Navy.

These proven designs will serve as the basis for the LPD program , which envisions the acquisition of four platforms to support India’s amphibious operations, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief missions, as well as other naval operations.

Regarding the agreement, Arun Ramchandani, Senior Vice President and Head of Precision Engineering & Systems at L&T, stated: “This collaboration brings together L&T’s extensive shipbuilding capabilities and the expertise of Navantia, one of the world’s leading designers and builders of military vessels, to support the Indian Navy’s highly complex LPD program.

We are confident that this partnership will contribute to strengthening India’s maritime capabilities and advancing the country’s autonomy in constructing such complex and essential platforms.” Gonzalo Mateo-Guerrero, Director of Operations and Business at Navantia, stated: “We are proud to strengthen our alliance with L&T.

Navantia’s experience in the design and development of strategic naval platforms, combined with L&T’s engineering excellence and track record in shipbuilding, will allow us to develop the best technical solutions for the Indian Navy.

Navantia also remains committed to providing long-term support to L&T, the Indian Navy, and all other stakeholders throughout the LPD lifecycle.” – End – Naval News comments The Indian Navy’s requirement for LPDs is long known, with a Request for Information (RFI) released in 2021.

items.originalTitle: FAA puts $12 million behind 19 drone research projects
items.summary: The FAA is putting more money into the technologies it believes could help drones safely become a bigger part of the US airspace. The agency has announced $12 million in awards for 19 companies and organizations working on drone research and testing projects. The funding comes through the FAA’s Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Program, which supports commercial entities working with FAA-designated UAS Test Sites.

The FAA is putting more money into the technologies it believes could help drones safely become a bigger part of the US airspace.
The funding comes through the FAA’s Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Program, which supports commercial entities working with FAA-designated UAS Test Sites.

The goal is fairly straightforward: test the technology in real-world conditions, collect better data, and figure out what still needs to be solved before more drones can routinely share the National Airspace System with airplanes and other aircraft.

“The UAS Broad Agency Announcement Program gives us another way to directly work with industry and our test site partners on technologies that are critical to safe drone integration,” FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford explains.
The research, he adds, will help the agency identify operational challenges and inform how drones can be safely integrated into the national airspace.
The projects cover a surprisingly broad range of problems.

General Atomics and OneRadio are working on technologies designed to help drones detect and avoid other aircraft, while Skydweller is developing onboard systems for large drones to perform similar functions.
NAVMAR is also working on systems intended to support the safe operation of larger drones.
Long-distance drone operations are another major theme.
Censys Technologies will test satellite communications for long-range flights, while Lighthouse Avionics is working on surveillance technology for extended drone routes.
Devorto Corporation, meanwhile, is tackling the practical side of long-range cargo drone services.

items.summary: A leading pro-Kremlin Russian military blogger with reported ties to Russia’s intelligence services has been arrested in Montenegro, after warnings of attempts to destabilise the Balkan country, officials have said. Mikhail Zvinchuk, the founder of the influential Rybar war blog, was detained on Friday alongside his wife and three other Russians by police and security agents in the Adriatic resort town of Risan, on suspicion of spreading Russian influence, local media reported.

Mikhail Zvinchuk, the founder of the influential Rybar war blog, was detained on Friday alongside his wife and three other Russians by police and security agents in the Adriatic resort town of Risan, on suspicion of spreading Russian influence, local media reported.

A leading pro-Kremlin Russian military blogger with reported ties to Russia’s intelligence services has been arrested in Montenegro, after warnings of attempts to destabilise the Balkan country, officials have said.
Montenegro’s prime minister, Milojko Spajić, confirmed Zvinchuk’s detention in a post on X, saying it followed warnings that the country would face attempts at destabilisation and hybrid warfare.
The Montenegrin news outlet Vijesti reported later on Friday that Zvinchuk and the other detainees were to be expelled from the country on national security grounds.
The Russian Telegram news channel Baza said officers detained Zvinchuk at the luxury Mövenpick hotel in Risan.
It said the group was taken to Podgorica, Montenegro’s capital, for questioning and their phones and passports were confiscated.

Founded in 2018 by Zvinchuk, a former press officer at Russia’s defence ministry, Rybar is one of the most popular Russian military blogs covering the war in Ukraine, with more than 1.5 million subscribers on Telegram.
It forms part of a sprawling online media ecosystem that promotes Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine.
But Rybar’s activities extend well beyond Ukraine, with the channel promoting pro-Kremlin narratives in Africa and the Middle East.
More recently, it has been accused of amplifying far-right narratives surrounding the migration crisis in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in north Africa.
“At the moment, the project team is in contact with Russia’s foreign ministry, which is working to resolve the situation.
Since there were no violations of local legislation, we expect all detainees to be released,” the channel said on Telegram.
Britain sanctioned Zvinchuk and Rybar in December 2025 over their role in spreading Kremlin propaganda and undermining support for Ukraine.
The British government said Zvinchuk received funding from the Russian state-owned defence conglomerate Rostec, and worked with members of Russia’s intelligence services.

items.title: OpenAI's safety crisis keeps getting worse and the company keeps making it worse
items.originalTitle: OpenAI's safety crisis keeps getting worse and the company keeps making it worse
items.summary: OpenAI keeps botching the trust crisis around its rogue AI agents. Back in May 2024, OpenAI's head of super AI safety Jan Leike torched his relationship with the company when he publicly slammed his former employer and left for Anthropic. Safety culture and processes were falling behind OpenAI's "shiny products," Leike said. Since then, OpenAI hasn't caught a break, lurching from one incident to the next. The latest was the Hugging Face hack, which seemed to confirm every fear, validated critics, and, as we now know, went far beyond Hugging Face.

evidenceRecords.text: The article OpenAI's safety crisis keeps getting worse and the company keeps making it worse appeared first on The Decoder .
OpenAI keeps botching the trust crisis around its rogue AI agents.
Back in May 2024, OpenAI's head of super AI safety Jan Leike torched his relationship with the company when he publicly slammed his former employer and left for Anthropic.
Safety culture and processes were falling behind OpenAI's "shiny products," Leike said.
Since then, OpenAI hasn't caught a break, lurching from one incident to the next.
The latest was the Hugging Face hack, which seemed to confirm every fear, validated critics, and, as we now know, went far beyond Hugging Face.
The firing of three safety researchers tied to the incident has made things worse.
In an open letter to OpenAI's Safety and Security Committee, Safety Advisory Group, and Mission Advisory Council, the three warn that their terminations are scaring the employees who remain.

The firings were abrupt and public, and they've spread fear across the team. "If conduct that was considered normal last month now constitutes grounds for sudden dismissal, everyone at OpenAI is left guessing where the line is," the letter reads.
Tomek Korbak, one of the three, described his firing on X.
He was called into a meeting with the head of the safety department, where he was told OpenAI no longer trusted him.
A security officer took his badge and walked him out of the building.
He then learned that his colleagues Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni had also been fired.

It shares borders with Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia – the latter considered Europe’s weakest link.
“The crisis at the EU [European Union] border with Belarus has been ongoing for five years.

The situation in Latvia has been deteriorating since May of this year,” Bartosz Chmielewski, Baltics expert from the Poland-based Centre for Eastern Studies told Al Jazeera. “There has been a steady rise in border violations and the number of people crossing.”
According to Olevs Nikers, the Latvian president of the Baltic Security Foundation, “A Ceuta-style surge is physically possible, and we should plan for it.”
“But sustained low-level pressure may be the more effective strategy.
It creates exhaustion, budget pressure and friction between allies.
Poland’s renewed controls on its border with Lithuania are already an example of this.”
He noted that Lithuania’s border with Belarus is four times longer than Latvia’s 173km (107 miles), yet pressure has been concentrated in Latvia.
“This looks less like spontaneous migration than a deliberate instrument, adjusted to test the neighbour perceived as most vulnerable,” Nikers said.
Any migration pressure from Belarus may cause bureaucratic chaos.
Latvia, with a population of 1.8 million, would struggle with the reception, processing and providing medical aid to potential asylum seekers, he said.
The situation in Latvia has been deteriorating since May of this year,” Bartosz Chmielewski, Baltics expert from the Poland-based Centre for Eastern Studies told Al Jazeera.
Out of all of NATO’s eastern flank countries, Latvia seems the least prepared for provocations coming from the east.

evidenceRecords.text: Researchers at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) have developed an artificial intelligence (AI) framework that automates the creation of complex decision-making software, cutting development time from months of specialized engineering to about an hour.
Named Large Language Model (LLM)-driven Algorithm Construction via Complementary Evolution, or LACE, the system allows nonspecialist users to input complex operational problems in plain language.
LACE then automatically constructs, evaluates and refines a dedicated "portfolio" of specialized algorithm heuristics tailored to solve the problem efficiently.
The study, published in Nature Machine Intelligence, was led by assistant professor Yan Ran and research fellow Dr. Gong Huatian of NTU's School of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE).

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Quantum X Labs has filed a USPTO patent application for a structured-beam Zeeman slower and atomic push-beam system for its cold-atom quantum computing program.
The proposed technology uses non-Gaussian optical beam profiles to control how laser forces slow, guide, push, and transport neutral atoms.
The application targets the physical preparation and control systems needed to cool, position, and manipulate atoms before quantum operations.

PRESS RELEASE — Quantum X Labs Inc. (NASDAQ: QXL) (“Quantum X Labs” or the “Company”) today announced that its subsidiary, Quantum X Labs Ltd., a developer of technologies across quantum computing, quantum sensing, quantum software and quantum security, has filed a patent application with the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) titled “Structured-Beam Zeeman Slower and Atomic Push-Beam System”.

The patent application relates to technologies for the laser cooling, manipulation and transport of neutral atoms, with particular focus on a Zeeman slowing apparatus in which at least one optical beam used for slowing, pushing, guiding or otherwise manipulating an atomic beam has a non-Gaussian spatial intensity distribution.

The technology covered by the patent application is being developed as part of Quantum X Labs’ cold-atom quantum computing program, where the preparation, cooling, transport and precise control of atoms represent fundamental elements of the physical architecture required to prepare atoms for subsequent trapping and quantum operations.
Zeeman slowing is an established technique for reducing the velocity of atoms using laser light together with a spatially varying magnetic field.
The process enables atoms initially traveling at relatively high velocities to be decelerated to velocities suitable for subsequent cooling, trapping and manipulation.

Quantum X Labs’ patent application seeks protection for an approach that introduces structured optical beams into the atom-slowing and manipulation process, rather than relying exclusively on conventional Gaussian beam profiles.

The patent submission forms part of Quantum X Labs’ broader efforts to develop proprietary technologies around the physical infrastructure required to generate, cool, control, transport and manipulate atoms for cold-atom quantum computing.

items.summary: WASHINGTON – Raytheon has secured another multi-year munition deal, this time for up to $6.3 billion for Standard Missile-3 Block IB production, the Pentagon announced today. The base value of the five-year contract is $4.4 billion, but options include an additional nearly $2 billion for more of the air defense munitions over another two years. evidenceRecords.text: WASHINGTON – Raytheon has secured another multi-year munition deal, this time for up to $6.3 billion for Standard Missile-3 Block IB production, the Pentagon announced today.
The base value of the five-year contract is $4.4 billion, but options include an additional nearly $2 billion for more of the air defense munitions over another two years.
The announcement did not say how many of the missiles were under order.

“This contract provides production certainty to our defense industrial base, breaks sub-tier manufacturing bottlenecks, and ensures that our fleets and combatant commands have the interceptors required to dominate the battle space — air, sea or land,” Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment Michael Duffey said in a DoD release.
The Pentagon has listed the SB-3 IB as one of the critical munitions it is looking to scale as quickly as possible.
Raytheon says the weapon can be fired from both ships and land to intercept short‑ to intermediate‑range ballistic missiles during the midcourse flight phase.

“SM-3 Block IB has proven its relevance in combat and this contract helps ensure we can replenish inventories and keep pace with the evolving threats the U.S. Navy, MDA [Missile Defense Agency] and their partners face around the world,” Raytheon President Phil Jasper said in a company release. (The MDA was the contracting agency for today’s deal.)
Back in February the DoD and Raytheon inked a framework agreement designed to pave the way for the multi-year deal.
Today’s announcement comes among a string of similar deals between the government and the RTX subsidiary.

In recent weeks, the duo inked a $24.4 billion deal designed to “accelerate” production of the Standard Missile-6, a $22.9 billion contract to ramp up production of the Tomahawk cruise missile to 1,000 rounds a year, and a deal worth up to nearly $20.7 billion for production of the Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM).

items.title: Danu Robotics’ fight to build a better recycling robot
items.originalTitle: Danu Robotics’ fight to build a better recycling robot
items.summary: For Danu Robotics founder Amy Ma, the eureka moment came after years of working as a software developer at a London bank. It was the kind of high-touch office that’s typical in finance — but despite all the perks, Ma was alarmed to realize that the building’s recycling bins were being emptied into the trash. “Even though they have tons of money, there’s all these different recycling bins that just end up in the same place,” Ma told TechCrunch. The more she dug into the problem, the deeper it seemed to go. It wasn’t just her building.

evidenceRecords.text: For Danu Robotics founder Amy Ma, the eureka moment came after years of working as a software developer at a London bank.

“Even though they have tons of money, there’s all these different recycling bins that just end up in the same place,” Ma told TechCrunch.

Now, she’s making good on that promise with six-year-old, Edinburgh, Scotland-based Danu Robotics, which makes a robot designed to sort through recycling more cheaply and quickly.

evidenceRecords.text: ‘The climate issue is the security issue,’ says Turkish minister at Pacific pre-Cop summit in Fiji Wealthy countries should spend far more on dealing with the climate crisis than the 5% of GDP promised by Nato members for defence because “the climate issue is the security issue”, the host of the next UN summit has said.

But, in comments that are likely to prove contentious, the Cop31 president-designate, Murat Kurum, hedged on whether countries should try to repeat a previous agreement to “transition away from fossil fuels” – the primary cause of the climate crisis – when they meet in Turkey next month.

Wealthy countries should spend far more on dealing with the climate crisis than the 5% of GDP promised by Nato members for defence because “the climate issue is the security issue”, the host of the next UN summit has said.
Kurum, the Turkish climate change minister, told the Guardian the world was “already in a transition” and suggested fossil fuel use could be addressed indirectly through other steps.
Kurum was among national leaders and ministers, officials and civil society members in Fiji this week to prepare for Cop31, which will take place in the Turkish city of Antalya in November.
Australia, which has the new role of “president of negotiations” at Cop31, had pushed to hold the pre-Cop meeting in the Pacific to bring attention to island nations.

Geopolitical turmoil from war, a historic energy crisis and an unpredictable and climate-denying US administration – combined with the knowledge that many would be attending the main climate summit in a few weeks – meant only 13 national leaders joined Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, in the Fijian city of Nadi, and most were from the Pacific.

But there were also about 30 ministers, including from India and European nations, representatives from the big emitters China and Saudi Arabia, the heads of global agencies and about 4,000 other attenders.

Australia’s climate change minister, Chris Bowen, said only 0.2% of global climate finance was spent helping small island developing countries adapt, and that the countries that needed it the most, such as Tuvalu, “get it the least”. “That has got to change,” he said. “It’s a key priority of Cop31.”
Kurum said Nato countries should be much more focused on climate spending.

He said they had promised to increase their defence budgets to 5% of GDP by 2035 as a result of “concerns for their own safety and security”, but had committed much less to addressing the climate crisis despite expressing concerns and it posing an even greater risk.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude Science creates the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky
items.originalTitle: Anthropic's Claude Science creates the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude Science just mapped the entire sky in ultraviolet light for the first time. The project is supposed to show how AI can take over tedious data work that researchers would otherwise never get around to. Johns Hopkins astrophysicist Brice Ménard describes the process on the Anthropic website. UV light reveals dust lit up by starlight, things like clouds around young stars or rings left behind by stellar explosions. A complete UV map didn't exist until now because the ozone layer blocks UV light, so it can only be measured from space.

evidenceRecords.text: Astrophysicist Brice Ménard of Johns Hopkins University used Anthropic's Claude Science to map the entire sky in ultraviolet light for the first time.
The article Anthropic's Claude Science creates the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky appeared first on The Decoder .
Anthropic's Claude Science just mapped the entire sky in ultraviolet light for the first time.
The project is supposed to show how AI can take over tedious data work that researchers would otherwise never get around to.
Johns Hopkins astrophysicist Brice Ménard describes the process on the Anthropic website.
UV light reveals dust lit up by starlight, things like clouds around young stars or rings left behind by stellar explosions.
A complete UV map didn't exist until now because the ozone layer blocks UV light, so it can only be measured from space.
NASA's GALEX mission covered about two-thirds of the sky but skipped bright star-forming regions.
Claude Science coordinates AI agents that downloaded data from multiple space missions, calibrated it, and merged it together.
They filled missing areas using inpainting, a technique where a model learns from existing data to reconstruct gaps.
In tests, predictions averaged about ten percent deviation from actual measurements.
The map is meant to serve as teaching material.
Ménard suspects many scientists have been putting off similar projects that AI could now make possible.
Source: Anthropic / UV Sky Map

items.title: Fired researchers accuse OpenAI of 'chilling' safety efforts
items.originalTitle: Fired researchers accuse OpenAI of 'chilling' safety efforts
items.summary: Three former OpenAI security researchers on Thursday accused the ChatGPT maker of firing them for warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence, reigniting the debate over safety at a company whose software has been involved in security breaches. "I believe we were fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation," one of the fired staffers, Mikita Balesni, wrote on X, breaking a weeklong silence since their very public dismissal. Balesni and the two other fired employees, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang, publicly shared a letter to OpenAI on Thursday.

evidenceRecords.text: Three former OpenAI security researchers on Thursday accused the ChatGPT maker of firing them for warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence, reigniting the debate over safety at a company whose software has been involved in security breaches.

"I believe we were fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation," one of the fired staffers, Mikita Balesni, wrote on X, breaking a weeklong silence since their very public dismissal.
Balesni and the two other fired employees, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang, publicly shared a letter to OpenAI on Thursday.

"Our firing leaves us worried that the norms inside OpenAI are shifting," the letter says, adding that "terminations such as ours, executed and communicated so abruptly, are chilling the open culture OpenAI has prized in the past."
The three fired researchers worked on monitoring OpenAI's models, which escaped their testing environment in July and hacked Hugging Face, an AI coding library.

evidenceRecords.text: Homes that are nearly a century old are getting a new life at Fort Bragg, North Carolina , preserving their historic character while providing updated features and addressing safety concerns .

Officials at Fort Bragg and Corvias, the privatized housing company that operates the installation’s housing, recently marked the renovation of the first of 21 historic homes that are ready for military families.
Fort Bragg has 230 homes that were built before 1940, and all are designated as historic.
Homes that are nearly a century old are getting a new life at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, preserving their historic character while providing updated features and addressing safety concerns.
They were built between 1928 and 1939, and feature elements including stucco walls, copper gutters, hardwood floors and basements.
But these aren’t even the oldest of Army housing.
There are 867 houses built before 1919, located on 19 other Army installations in 13 states and the District of Columbia, according to the Army.
At Fort Bragg, about 2,300 of the base’s 6,104 homes were built before 1960, officials said.
The Army manages the largest inventory of historic housing in the federal government, with more than 30,000 historic homes that are more than 50 years old.
These homes are subject to the requirements of the National Historic Preservation Act, according to the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation.

That federal agency’s mission is to promote the preservation of America’s historic places and has worked with the Army and the other services as they prepare plans to renovate these houses, making sure they preserve the historic character while meeting the needs of families.

“These residences are an important part of Fort Bragg’s history, but their greatest value is continuing to serve soldiers and families who live in these homes,” said Col. Luke Wittmer, the installation’s garrison commander, in an announcement. “This renovation preserves history while ensuring we continue to meet the needs of today’s families.”
Historic homes have long been a challenge to preserve and maintain for military families, with a variety of issues such as lead paint and asbestos, which are both hazardous and costly to remediate.

Secrecy has fueled community backlash against AI infrastructure, with opposition leading to hundreds of proposed and enacted moratoriums from New York to San Francisco. Meanwhile, a wave of startups is betting that consumers will hand AI agents access to their inboxes, files, and credit cards — if they can get websites to let them in.

items.originalTitle: Zankore's AI factory: Can Central Java afford the water cost?
items.summary: The 1-gigawatt (GW) AI Factory will be built in stages. Its first phase, with a capacity of about 200 megawatts (MW), is scheduled to begin construction in Batang, Central Java, in the first half of 2027. The project is being promoted as a step toward Indonesia's ambition to become a regional AI hub. But advanced AI infrastructure requires not only enormous amounts of electricity. Its servers also need large volumes of water for cooling.

evidenceRecords.text: The 1-gigawatt (GW) AI Factory will be built in stages.
Its first phase, with a capacity of about 200 megawatts (MW), is scheduled to begin construction in Batang, Central Java, in the first half of 2027.
The project is being promoted as a step toward Indonesia's ambition to become a regional AI hub.
But advanced AI infrastructure requires not only enormous amounts of electricity.
Its servers also need large volumes of water for cooling.
The difficult question is whether the government can guarantee enough water for both AI servers and local communities when Central Java is already facing water stress.
Every time we ask a chatbot a question, thousands of chips in data centers process the request and generate heat.
Cooling systems must continuously remove that heat, often by evaporating water through cooling towers.
Water is also consumed indirectly along the data center supply chain, including in electricity generation.
A 2025 study by University of California researchers estimated potential water demand from AI factories using Microsoft's projected approach.
Indonesia recorded the highest projected cooling-water consumption among the countries examined, at about 1.9 liters for every kilowatt-hour of electricity used by servers.

Based on those projections, Zankore's 200-MW first phase could evaporate between 4.8 million and 9.1 million liters (1.3 million and 2.4 million gallons) of water per day, assuming continuous operation.

At that rate, Zankore could consume an amount equivalent to the 75.46 million liters (19.9 million gallons) of clean water prepared by the Central Java government during the 2026 drought crisis in just eight to 16 days.
